name: Philippus de Harveng
claimNotes: Entire corpus untranslated. Known works include Responsio de damnatione Salomonis, Life of Augustine of Hippo, and theological writings.

name: Atto Vercellensis
claimNotes: Polypticum, De pressuris ecclesiasticis, biblical commentaries—corpus untranslated.

name: Bruno Herbipolensis
claimNotes: Psalterium beati Brunonis episcopi herbipolensis (entire work).

name: Landulfus Sagax
claimNotes: Historia Romana/Historia Miscella—primary work remains untranslated.

name: Ado Viennensis
claimNotes: Chronicon (Breviarium chronicorum) and Martyrologium remain untranslated; based on Bede's chronicle with original synthesis

name: Ernaldus Bonaevallis
claimNotes: De ultimis verbis domini, De septem verbis Domini in cruce, other theological works

name: Bernaldus Constantiensis
claimNotes: All 14 works appear to remain in Latin; manuscript editions available at Documenta Catholica Omnia

name: Goffridus Vindocinensis
claimNotes: Sermons, hymns, theological tracts, and letters remain in Latin; Sirmondiana edition standard but Latin only

name: Oddo Astensis
claimNotes: Expositio in Psalmos (dedicated to Bruno of Asti/Segni, PL 165) remains untranslated in Latin

name: Arnulfus Lexoviensis
claimNotes: Works in PL 201 - primarily letters and other ecclesiastical writings remain in Latin

name: Marianus Scottus
claimNotes: Chronicon Scotorum/Chronicle remains untranslated to English; extensive medieval use by Florence of Worcester and English chroniclers

name: Landulfus Mediolanensis
claimNotes: Historia Mediolanensis (1050-1083) untranslated; important for Milan history despite inaccuracies

name: Claudius Taurinensis
claimNotes: Biblical commentaries (Genesis, Matthew, Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Exodus, Leviticus, Ruth-Kings, Joshua-Judges) all untranslated

name: Hericus Antissiodorensis
claimNotes: Works of Henry of Auxerre (Haimo) remain untranslated; biblical commentaries on various books untranslated

name: Wandalbertus Prumiensis
claimNotes: Martyrology in verse (c. 848), Life of St. Goar, supplementary poems on months, agricultural labor, seasons, church Hours

name: Egbertus Eboracensis
claimNotes: Works attributed in Middle Ages (Paenitentiale Ecgberhti, pontifical, canons) not authenticated by modern scholars; no English translation

name: Folcardus Sithivensis
claimNotes: Hagiographer (fl. 1080); Miracula Sancti Bertini; works preserved in Latin only

name: Lupus de Olmeto
claimNotes: Regula monachorum ex scriptis Hieronymi collecta (15th c.); manuscripts at Bodleian and BnF; no English translation

name: Adrianus II
claimNotes: Pope Adrian II (792–872); diplomatic and papal correspondence; no dedicated English translation of his works
